findings.finding: Every broad Q3 2026 demand series NIBE's Climate Solutions sells into is strong: Swedish heat pump sales +22% y/y with ground-source (NIBE's core) +30%, German subsidy applications +103% (Aug) and +34% (Sep), and Carrier reports European residential heat pump sales up ~35%, pointing to organic growth at or above the 8.7-11% analysts model.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: sales 10,849m vs ~10,553m consensus and EBIT 15% above, stock +8.8%; Q1 2026: sales -0.2% reported, stock -7.4%; Q3 2025 sales/EBIT in line after a pre-print rally, stock -13.0%.
findings.original_quote: Försäljningen av värmepumpar i Sverige ökade med 22 procent under tredje kvartalet 2026 ... Störst var ökningen för vätska-vattenvärmepumpar, där försäljningen steg med 30 procent. (Swedish heat pump sales rose 22% in Q3 2026 ... the largest increase was in liquid-to-water [ground-source] heat pumps, up 30%.)
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: consensus has been raised (SB1 +1-2%, Citi raised, SEB to buy) and the stock is +11% over 60 days; Citi explicitly says the market already expects a strong report. What is left is the gap between broad series running +22-35% and consensus organic growth of ~9-11%; if fully priced, consensus would sit well above Citi's 1.49bn rather than 3% below it.
findings.independence: German BMWK subsidy data https://borsvarlden.com/artiklar/tyska-ansokningar-om-varmepumpssubventioner-steg-34-procent-pa-arsbasis-i-september ; Carrier Q3 2026 https://finviz.com/news/411135/carrier-reports-third-quarter-2026-results ; Ariston Q3 2026 'strong heating growth in Europe thanks to heat pumps' https://www.aristongroup.com/content/dam/aristoninvestors/documents/press-releases/20261104%20Ariston%20Q3%20and%209M%202026%20Results%20Press%20Release_EN.pdf

findings.finding: The company's own seasonal pattern implies a Q3 margin slightly above consensus: in 2025 the operating margin stepped from 9.4% (Q2) to 11.3% (Q3) on flat sales; the same +1.9pp on Q2 2026's 11.4% gives ~13.3% on ~11.05bn sales, ~1.47bn EBIT vs a ~1.43-1.45bn bar (consensus margin ~13.0%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The EBIT beat/miss has set the sign on the last two prints: Q2 2026 +15% EBIT beat -> +8.8%; Q3 2025 EBIT 1,140m vs 1,145m expected -> -13.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference from two primary documents (Q2 2026 report: 1,232m / 11.4%; Q3 2025 CEO comment: 11.3% from 9.2%, Q2 2025 944m on 10,082m), not a disclosed number. Consensus at ~13.0% already assumes most of the step; the residual is ~2% of EBIT. Higher depreciation this year (CEO, Q2) and input-cost inflation could absorb it.
findings.independence: SEB's upgrade cites higher capacity utilisation as upside to consensus https://borsvarlden.com/artiklar/seb-ser-attraktiv-uppsida-i-nibe-hojer-till-kop ; Q3 2025 base https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bfdacc67e2cb081c7afaba22b0283888a&lang=en&src=listed

findings.finding: Input and logistics cost inflation accelerated in Q3 2026: Ariston (direct European heating peer) reported 'accelerating inflation in input and logistics costs', a like-for-like margin down 30bp and cut its FY organic guide to +1-2%; SB1 flags rising raw-material prices and limited room for price increases at NIBE.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin/outlook disappointment drove the -13.0% on Q3 2025 (in-line numbers, cautious outlook) and the -7.4% on Q1 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer proxy, not a NIBE statement; the sell-side previews (Citi, Inderes) model margin expansion to ~13% without mentioning cost inflation, and only SB1 flags it. If priced, the Q3 margin estimates would have been trimmed rather than raised in November.
